qualification: Indicative local loopback results. Foreground CPU activity increased during the final three-server matrix; all rows retained. Compare paired controls within a run, not absolute rates across phases. Diagnostic instrumented timings excluded from speed claims. No confidence interval or general ranking is claimed.
fixture: Bounded async application: one 1 MiB write then complete; 128-byte control uses synchronous output. TLS 1.3 AES-128-GCM. Native generator performs body-hash probes before/after load; fairness client hashes every completed body.

decisions.conclusion: All seven experimental production changes were discarded. The production source remains identical to fdeb0518; four regression cases and a configurable stream-window fairness benchmark are retained.

experiments.name: Owner DATA continuation (v1)
experiments.reason: Reduced CPU but worsened same-connection foreground p99 on both JDKs; no bulk throughput improvement.

experiments.name: Owner continuation with pending-input guard (v2)
experiments.reason: The pending-input guard did not resolve the same-connection latency regression. No saturated bulk trial was needed after this fairness failure.

experiments.name: Owner continuation yielding between selector visits (v3)
experiments.reason: About 9% more bulk throughput and 21–22% less CPU, but foreground p99 worsened about 18% on Java 21 and 16% on Java 25.

experiments.name: Owner continuation with single-open-stream guard (v4)
experiments.reason: About 7–9% more bulk throughput and 21–22% less CPU, but foreground p99 worsened about 23% on Java 21 and 20% on Java 25.

experiments.name: Reader applies valid credit (credit)
experiments.reason: Writer dispatches fell 14–19%; initial bulk CPU fell about 5%, but matched-rate results were mixed. The 65535-byte-window mixed-stream control raised p99 in all four pairs: medians +5.5% on Java 21 and +1.9% on Java 25, with scheduled latency also higher. The additional credit-processing path is not justified by these tradeoffs.

experiments.name: Coalesce credit notifications (notifications)
experiments.reason: Dispatch counts were essentially unchanged and CPU changed only -0.1% / -0.5% with overlapping ranges. Additional deferred-notification state was not justified.

experiments.name: Reader credit shortcut with buffered-frame guard (credit-guard)
experiments.reason: In a fresh paired 65535-byte-window control, actual-send p99 was flat on Java 21 and 2.1% higher on Java 25; scheduled p99 was 1.9% / 5.2% higher. No clear fairness win was established. No further saturated throughput measurements were run after this check.

decisions.interpretation: These short local results do not prove universal latency ratios or identify where all mixed-stream queueing occurs. The conservative selection avoids adopting unproven tradeoffs. Diagnostic instrumentation is used for dispatch counts only; every unprofiled result, including adverse and mixed controls, is retained.
